The Cortex-M7 FPU supports estimation and small policies at 250 Hz. SD logging preserves raw sensor and control traces. Power transients and blocking writes can violate the loop deadline; current and mass are estimates.

Gyros track angular rates; accelerometers measure specific force, not gravity alone during thrust. Bias and axis alignment matter for attitude estimation. Rigid alignment and vibration characterization are needed before trusting this sensor.

Ambient pressure provides a height estimate through an atmosphere model. Static ports must avoid stagnation and wake pressure. Burn-time acceleration does not directly invalidate pressure, but airflow and filtering can bias and delay the reading.

ADXL375 +/-200 g accelerometer records launch acceleration that clips the low-g IMU. The low-g IMU still supplies gyro and fine acceleration. Noise, timing, alignment, wiring and data fusion require bench calibration; range alone does not qualify the sensor.
The log card records raw sensors, estimates, commands, fault state and supply voltage. Buffered writes and recovery from a full or failed card must preserve the control deadline.

A 2S pack supplies regulator headroom through discharge. Servo current spikes can brown out logic unless rails and decoupling are sized correctly. Capacity, mass and discharge rating are estimates pending a selected cell and measurements.
